 Real Madrid star scores twice to erase Japan’s early 2-goal lead, but Sakamoto strikes late to secure victory in Singapore Halis Sunnetci 14 November 2026 • Update : 14 November 2026 ISTANBUL Japan secured a dramatic 3-2 victory over Brazil in an international friendly on Saturday, with Tatsuhiro Sakamoto scoring a stoppage-time winner after Vinicius Junior’s brace had brought the South American side back from two goals down.
 Playing at Singapore National Stadium, Japan raced into an early 2-0 lead before the Real Madrid winger scored twice to bring Brazil level, only for the Samurai Blue to snatch victory in the closing moments.
 Japan broke the deadlock in the 15th minute when Ritsu Doan won possession near the halfway line and played through Takefusa Kubo, who drove into the penalty area before firing a left-footed shot into the bottom-right corner.
 The Asian side doubled their advantage just four minutes later as Shuto Nakano surged down the right flank and delivered a cutback for Keito Nakamura, who calmly finished past Brazilian goalkeeper Pedro Morisco.
 Brazil responded in the 33rd minute through Vinicius, who unleashed a spectacular long-range strike into the top-left corner after being picked out by Bruno Guimaraes.
 Japan took a 2-1 lead into halftime.
 Brazil continued to push for an equalizer after the break and finally found one in the 75th minute when Vinicius collected a short corner from Guimaraes, cut inside Yukinari Sugawara and struck a superb effort that hit the woodwork before crossing the line.
 However, Japan had the final say in the first minute of stoppage time.
 A deflected effort fell into the path of substitute Sakamoto on the right side of the penalty area, and the winger lifted a right-footed finish into the top-left corner to restore Japan’s lead.
 Brazil head coach Carlo Ancelotti and forward Raphinha were sent off following protests over an alleged foul on Joao Gomes in the buildup to the winning goal.
 The late goal sealed a 3-2 victory for Hajime Moriyasu’s side, leaving Brazil empty-handed despite Vinicius’ two spectacular goals.
 The result marked Japan’s second victory over Brazil, having secured their first in October 2025 before losing to the South Americans at the 2026 World Cup.
